cards.text: This is a psalm of David, the shepherd who beat Goliath (1 Samuel 17), written for the choirmaster. A whole group speaks to one person, and the first thing they say is, "May the LORD answer you in the day of trouble…" It's like the group chat blowing up your phone with good wishes before a rough day, except this group chat has a CHOIR.

cards.question: Next comes the name of the God of Jacob, the man God renamed Israel (Genesis 32:28). What does the group hope that name will do for the person in trouble?

cards.text: Next they tell this person, "May He send you help from the sanctuary and sustain you from Zion." Help straight from God's own house, with no hold music and no 'please leave a message.'
Then they hope He'll remember every gift this person has given. Not SOME of the gifts, friend. ALL of them.

cards.question: The group hopes the LORD will remember this person's gifts. True or false: they also hope He'll look favorably on this person's burnt offerings.

cards.text: Then a Selah lands right there in the song. After it, they tell this person they hope He'll give them the desires of their heart.

cards.question: The group hopes God will give this person the desires of their heart. What do they hope for this person's plans?
The group pictures the day this person wins. True or false: they hope they'll get to keep it quiet.

cards.text: They hope they'll get to shout for joy and raise a banner in the name of their God, like a whole stadium waving one giant flag.

cards.question: The group has one more hope for this person before the psalm changes direction. What do they hope the LORD will grant?

cards.text: Up to now, it's been one 'may' after another. Then the psalm says, "Now I know that the LORD saves His anointed; He answers him from His holy heaven with the saving power of His right hand."

cards.question: With 'Now I know,' the psalm turns from hoping to being ___.

cards.text: Then the psalm says, "Some trust in chariots and others in horses…" You know when somebody brags about their car's horsepower, and it still sits in rush hour traffic like everybody else's?

cards.question: Not chariots, not horses. The group says they trust in the ___ of the LORD their God.
The ones who trust in chariots and horses collapse and fall. True or false: the ones who trust in the name of the LORD fall right beside them.

cards.text: The psalm says, "They collapse and fall, but we rise up and stand firm." Friend, standing firm is the ONE thing I've got down, because I come with my own gold base.

cards.question: In the last line, the group calls on the LORD to save someone. Who is it?

cards.text: They say, "O LORD, save the king. Answer us on the day we call." The song opened hoping the LORD would answer one person, and it closes asking Him to answer all of them.
